reachable: Yes — verified end to end, including the failure mode that was fatal before. The head's contribution is added to the OUTPUT prediction at command positions (`new_pred[:, 0::2][:, :n] += contrib`), gated only by the command-validity mask `vc`, never by observation presence. The write is gated by `act = vc & vo` (off at the read step, where the observation is absent), but the READ `r_i = bmm(ks_i, mem)` is not gated at all and happens before both writes at step i, so the mechanism is fully live at the scored position. Executed check with a nonzero out_scale on the real r18 arch and a scoring-shaped layout: the prediction at the read position changes by 1.0027 (row r=3) and 0.3029 (row r=2); perturbing obs_t by 50x changes the prediction at cmd position t by exactly 0.0 while later positions move by 1.78/2.46 — both of the author's "verified numerically" claims hold exactly, as does "wrapped == unwrapped at init" (max abs diff 0.0, not merely 1e-6). Gradient: on a real-encoder batch, out_scale gets 4.07e-3 from the main loss alone; displace.weight and addr_in.weight get exactly 0.0 from the main loss (out_scale is zero-init, so nothing upstream of contrib sees main-loss gradient) and 4.298 / 17.18 from the aux, which does fire on this data (262 content-free steps, 62 pairs, 23 hop-1 align examples). One dead corner: read_gate.weight has exactly 0.0 gradient at init from both losses (it multiplies out_scale=0 in contrib and the aux uses ungated reads_t), so it only becomes live after out_scale moves — a slow start, not a break. Off-by-one caveat in divergence 1: the head cannot reach the read for a row at the layout's maximum r; no eligible window is at that r today.
solves_outside_model: No. The head file contains no string handling whatsoever — grep for split/find/startswith/cmds/json/open over the impl returns only the word "commands" inside the DESCRIPTION text. Every mining decision (dup_o, dup_c, content-free, pair selection, hop counting, align positives) is made from squared distances between the standardized embeddings already in the batch, and it produces only INDICES that select terms in a LOSS. The model's inputs are never mutated: `mod.run` reads `tok_emb` and the injection is added to the returned prediction tensor, computed causally from the same token stream the model sees (memory at step i contains writes from steps < i only). The stream axis is baseline_interleave with no code_cmds, so the read token is byte-identical under the native and role-swapped chains and the prior-retraction shape (resolved identity stamped into the scored read token) is structurally absent. This is legitimate loss shaping, not resolved routing reaching the model as input.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says. Every claim I could execute checked out, several to the digit. Wrapped == unwrapped at init is exact (0.0, not just 1e-6). The prediction at a command position is exactly invariant to that step's own observation, verified with a 50x perturbation on the real arch — so the mechanism is NOT switched off at the read the way an observation-gated mechanism would be. The head's memory read is ungated and precedes both writes; only the writes are gated by observation presence, which costs nothing at the last step. The jail audit reproduces essentially exactly under the real pinned encoder (I re-encoded all 724 steps with enc/e5-nocwd rather than a stand-in): 262/262 content-free steps flagged with zero false positives and zero false negatives, 62 pairs mined, 61 byte-identical, later ends cvar_test 37 / cups_test 19. The mining function is bit-identical to the parent's. There is no command-string parsing anywhere in the head; all supervision is embedding-distance mining that selects loss terms, and nothing resolved reaches the model as input, so this is not the retracted shape. Five minor divergences, none affecting the score as measured: (1) an off-by-one that makes the head a no-op at the read for any row sitting at the layout's maximum r — verified numerically, and zero eligible windows are at that r today (max r = 28, deepest eligible r = 25), but it is a latent bug that a deeper re-mint would activate; (2) the inherited transition aux runs at half the parent's global weight with a shorter ramp, which "weighted the same way" glosses over; (3) 22 of 23 hop-1 align examples get the intended source/destination labelling, not 23 of 23; (4) the stated aux magnitude (~0.7-1.8 vs main ~1) is ~2.8x main at full ramp on a real-encoder batch (3.82 vs 1.34); (5) the motivating claim that r18's memories "write at the same key they read" is wrong in detail (they use separate read/write projections) though right in substance (they write the step's own observation, never a retrieved value). Timing is 1.27-1.33x rather than the claimed 1.42x on this CPU, i.e. the claim is conservative. On the author's own stated load-bearing bet, which they could not test: with the real encoder `mv A B` and `mv B A` pool to cosine 0.9955 (squared distance 3.2% of the distance between two different mv commands), yet a linear probe recovers argument order at 83.9% held out — the order signal exists but is a very thin slice of the command embedding, so the bet is live and the author characterized it honestly.

divergences.claim: "the injected contribution ... is added to the arch's own prediction" at every command position — i.e. the mechanism is live at the scored read.
divergences.what_the_code_does: `run()` sets n = L//2 and `_forward` adds contrib only to cmd positions [:n]. The cups scoring layout has ODD L (= 2*max_r + 1), so the 0::2 view holds max_r+1 command positions while contrib holds only max_r. The LAST command position (index max_r) never receives the head's contribution, so for any row whose read sits at r == max_r the head is a structural no-op at the scored position.
divergences.evidence: Executed /tmp/.../reach.py: r18 net wrapped, out_scale randomized, L=11 (max_r=5). Diff at read position: row with r=5 -> 0.0; r=3 -> 1.0027; r=2 -> 0.3029. Quantified on the real inner-val slice (fedora+mariadb of dockerfs3-cupsF-treat/val.jsonl): 640 cups_test windows, max r = 28 (Lmax = 57 -> n = 28); the deepest depth>=3 core window has r = 25. So ZERO eligible windows are affected today and the score is unchanged — but a re-mint with a longer trajectory would silently switch the head off at the read for the deepest rows.

divergences.claim: "I keep ... the whole aux it was built around ... mined the same way and weighted the same way."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The mining is bit-identical, and the two arms keep their relative weights (cos 0.10, mse 0.02, mem_arm_w 0.5). But the transition aux's GLOBAL scale is halved relative to the parent (parent aux_weight 1.0 -> candidate aux_weight 0.5 multiplying the whole thing) and its ramp is shortened (ramp_steps 400 -> 300). The parent's aux is therefore not reproduced at its original strength.
divergences.evidence: Executed /tmp/.../minediff.py: `HD._mine_path_triples` returns tensors bit-equal to `CH._mine_triples` on the same inputs (identical: True). Weights: r18_transition_forwardmodel_consistency._DEFAULTS has aux_weight 1.0 / ramp_steps 400; the candidate's _DEFAULTS have aux_weight 0.5 / ramp_steps 300 and multiply the transition block by aux_weight*ramp. The author does state 0.5 and 300 explicitly later in the hypothesis, so this is incomplete disclosure rather than a false statement.

divergences.claim: "all 23 hops==1 cases put a cvar_op / mv step in the middle whose source path is the i-command's path and whose destination path is the j-command's path."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Under the real pinned encoder, 22 of 23 hop-1 cases have that property. The 23rd pairs two different `ls` commands whose directory listings happen to be byte-identical, with an unrelated `mv /tmp/w/cups/g22/f252.dat.4 /tmp/w/cups/var/lib/misc/state.db.5` as the middle step — so that align example receives a source/destination labelling that is not the i/j paths.
divergences.evidence: Executed /tmp/.../realmine.py: encoded all 724 jail steps with enc/e5-nocwd via enc_e5_base_nocwd render/pool, standardized, ran the module's own mining. Every other audited number reproduces EXACTLY: 262/262 empty-output steps flagged content-free, 0 false positives, 0 false negatives; 62 pairs mined, 61 byte-identical; later ends cvar_test 37 (18+10+9) and cups_test 19, matching the hypothesis to the unit.

divergences.claim: "The aux is roughly the size of the main loss at full ramp (measured ~0.7-1.8 on real-structured batches, against a main MSE near 1)."
divergences.what_the_code_does: At full ramp on a real-encoder jail batch the aux is ~2.8x the main loss, not ~1x. It will fall as the InfoNCE terms train (log(#candidates) ~ 3.4 per term at init), but the stated range is not what the code produces at the start of the ramp — which is the regime the author's own clipping concern is about.
divergences.evidence: Executed /tmp/.../gradcheck.py with real-encoder embeddings for the 24 jail sequences, st['step'] forced to full ramp: main MSE 1.3447, aux 3.8230. /tmp/.../realmine.py separately gives the transport term alone at 3.911 before aux_weight. Note the author had no torch in the jail, so this measured number could not have been executed.

divergences.claim: "The r18 arch cannot do this today: both of its memories write a value at the SAME key they read (path_read/path_write over one hidden state ...)."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The file and path delta-rule memories use SEPARATE read and write projections — `q_file = quotient(file_read(x_cmd))` vs `k_file = quotient(file_write(x_cmd))`, and `q_path = unit(path_read(h_cmd0))` vs `k_path = unit(path_write(h_cmd0))` — so read key and write key are already distinct there. The substantive point survives for a different reason: those memories write value_path = the step's own observation, never a value retrieved from another slot; and only `_transition_reads` genuinely uses one key `p` for both read and write.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/arch/r18_pathstate_latent_transition_worldmodel.py lines 73-80 (file_read/file_write, path_read/path_write are four distinct nn.Linear), 324-334 (q!=k passed to _chunked_delta_reads), 331 (value_path = obs_tok), 250-271 (_transition_reads uses `pi` for both the read bmm and the write outer product). This is a claim about the parent arch's code, not about the candidate's own code.
